title: Prompt flags
summary: Short flags in a message (-d, -w, -nc, -q, -rc, -a, -p, -m, -nb, -away) change how Claude handles it.
details: Short tokens you put at the start or end of a message change how Claude handles it: -d discussion only, -w search the web first, -nc no commits, -q ask when unclear, -rc extra rigor, -a deep analysis, -p plan mode, -m remember it permanently, -nb new branch, plus -away. It is for steering a single message without long instructions. It adds one plain-text rule file under ~/.claude/rules/ that loads into every session; no code runs and no network is used.
trigger: Add a flag such as -d, -w, -q, -rc, -a, -p, -m or -nb at the start or end of your message.
risk: Text only, loaded into every session. No code runs.
